verbatim_or_table: Specifications Table (Data in Brief companion): 'Markov chain Monte Carlo simulation of the productivity for the US through 2030 of the current durable cell and gene therapy development pipeline'. Data source location: Pharmaprojects|Informa 2021 database; Clinicaltrials.gov; AACT; SEER; academic and gray literature. 'Data were extracted manually from the Pharmaprojects, clinicaltrials.gov and SEER databases, using purpose written SQL code from the AACT database, and from both gray and academic literature.' Collection period 2018-2021.
notes: Read in the Data in Brief companion (PMC8844867) full text at Europe PMC. Exact calendar date of the pipeline snapshot used in the DDT model is not stated in the Data in Brief summary; Mendeley dataset v1 published 10 Dec 2021 (doi 10.17632/djm65zrhmt.1).

source_title: Durable cell and gene therapy potential patient and financial impact: US projections of product approvals, patients treated, and product revenues
verbatim_or_table: Qualifying (durable) therapies: '(i) employ or modify DNA or RNA, (ii) are administered in a single course, and (iii) are expected to deliver at least 18 months average benefit'. Modalities: gene replacement therapies (in vivo/ex vivo, viral vectors); CAR-T cells and TCR-engineered immune cells; gene editing (ZFNs, TALENs, CRISPR-Cas9); long-acting DNA plasmids.
notes: Data in Brief companion.

verbatim_or_table: Adoption: Bass diffusion model (parameters in dataset FD4 'Incidence, Prevalence, Adoption') incorporating disease severity, economics and friction between stakeholders. '20% of patients enrolled in acute lymphoblastic leukemia (ALL) and diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) late-stage trials did not receive an infusion' hence a peak adoption level of 75% applied to all oncology treatments, with an assumed time to peak of 2 years.
notes: Data in Brief companion. Forecasting datasets: FD1 Clinical Trials Data; FD2 Preclinical Data; FD3 Genes & Antigens; FD4 Incidence, Prevalence, Adoption.

These data were extracted from Pharmaprojects and clinicaltrials.gov in September 2018.' Phases: Phase 1, Phase 2 (incl. Phase 1/2), Phase 3 (incl. Phase 2/3); preclinical duration = first appearance on Pharmaprojects to first clinical trial. Success = '(i) commencement of a trial of a more advanced phase or (ii) submission of a New Drug Application (NDA) or a Biologics License Application (BLA)'. Multi-indication trials counted once per disease state.
notes: Numerical success probabilities are not printed in the brief.

source_title: MIT NEWDIGS Research Brief 2020F207-v051 Pipeline Analysis: Updated projection of US durable cell and gene therapies product-indication approvals based on December 2019 development pipeline
verbatim_or_table: Model: Markov Chain Monte Carlo; 100,000 iterations; for each development program the year of approval (if any) is summed across programs to create a product-indication approval projection. Exclusions: 'Mesenchymal stem cell therapies and those utilizing unmodified tumor infiltrating leukocytes are not included in our forecasting set.' Qualifying modalities: gene replacement (in vivo/ex vivo viral vectors), TCRs and CAR-engineered immune cells, gene editing (ZFN, TALEN, CRISPR-Cas9), long-acting DNA plasmids, with durable effects beyond 18 months.
notes: Projection of approvals only; the brief gives no patients-treated or revenue series.

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Abstract: 'To evaluate the potential impact of cell and gene therapies (CGTs) in France by forecasting the number of patients that will be treated with CGTs over the period 2023-2030 by therapeutic area and region ... Up to 44 new CGTs are forecasted to launch in France in the period 2023-2030, which translates into more than 69,400 newly treated patients in 2030.' Results text: 'An increase in CGT launches is forecasted from 2023 to 2027, followed by a decline after 2027.' 'the projected annual number of treated patients increases from 1,653 in 2023 to more than 69,400 patients by 2030'.
notes: Figures: Fig 2 launches per year; Fig 3 newly treated patients per year; Fig 4 annual treated patients by therapy area. Tables: T1 authorized CGTs in France at 31 Dec 2022; T2 probability of success; T3 launches by therapy area; T4 annual treated patients by therapy area.

verbatim_or_table: Pipeline snapshot: 'Data extraction covered all the trial information available in December 2022.' 'The mapping of the CGT clinical development pipeline led to the identification of 749 individual clinical trial programs for 419 CGTs in 38 indications' (327 Phase I, 367 Phase II, 55 Phase III studies).
notes: Pipeline snapshot December 2022.

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Probability of success (Table 2, based on MIT Project ALPHA): Phase I 10.8%; Phase II 16.0%; Phase III 44.1% (probability of reaching launch from the given phase).

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Launch timing: 'the assumed duration from Phase I, Phase II and Phase III to launch were 9, 7, and 5 years, respectively' (base scenario); 'the duration for the pessimistic and optimistic launch scenarios has a 1-year difference from the base launch'; 'Forecasted CGT launches across three scenarios are shown in the Supplementary Figure 1.'
notes: Scenario values for pessimistic/optimistic launches are only in Supplementary Figure 1 (not in the main text or XML tables) - see gap row.

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Adoption/uptake: historical adoption rates of launched CGTs 'ranged from 1 to 30%'; model assumes 'an estimated 1% adoption rate for each product in year one of launch, with incremental increases of 1% per year to a maximum of 6% in year six'. Treatment centres in France (2022): 0.046 per 100,000 population; 0.0543 per 1,000 square km.

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Baseline: 'As of 31 December 2022, 13 cell and gene therapies (CGTs), defined as gene therapy medicinal products and somatic cell therapies, excluding tissue-engineered therapies, were granted a European marketing authorization.' 'Out of these, 10 have been reimbursed or received early access authorization (AAP) in France, as shown in Table 1.'

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Exclusions: 'Trials with therapies that did not involve gene modification (e.g., human stem cell transplantation without genetic modification, or other forms of cellular transplantation) were excluded.' Patient-based epidemiological forecast (Figure 1): eligible population per indication x probability of success x launch timing x adoption.
notes: 'Newly treated patients' is not explicitly defined as incident vs prevalent in the text.

source_title: Forecasting the potential impact of cell and gene therapies in France: projecting product launches and patients treated
verbatim_or_table: Supplementary Figure 1 (three scenarios) - values not in main text
notes: Supplementary material not retrieved; only the +-1 year timing shift is described.

source_title: Cell and Gene therapy (CGT) pipeline deep dive (Paying for Cures, Center for Biomedical System Design / NEWDIGS, Tufts Medical Center)
verbatim_or_table: Web page 'Cell and Gene therapy (CGT) pipeline deep dive', Center for Biomedical System Design (NEWDIGS), Tufts Medical Center, Paying for Cures / Defining disruption section. 'Pipeline data through December 2023 are found below.' No explicit page date; Figure 2 and Table 1 image files are dated 2025/06 in their upload paths. Links on page: slides 'Overview of the CGT pipeline' (July 2023 PDF); research brief 'Are Cell and Gene Therapy programs a better bet?' (2023F210v056); Young et al 2022 (S16); JMCP 2025 pediatric-onset rare disease projection (doi 10.18553/jmcp.2025.31.5.491).
notes: The ICER-NEWDIGS white paper (April 2024) cites this page as accessed 2 Aug 2023 with different figures (48,000 patients/yr by 2030; 85 gene therapies by 2032), so the page has been revised at least once; the current text and the Figure 2 data table also differ from each other (see notes on those rows).

unit: treatable patients per year (US, all CGT)
verbatim_or_table: By 2032, the treatable patient population for CGT is anticipated to be 105,000+ patients per year.
notes: Page text. Also: treatment of the prevalent population expected to 'peak in 2031 and 2032, then decline'. The Figure 2 data table on the same page gives total patients treated of 98,195 in 2032 and a peak of 101,968 in 2034, so the '105,000+' text statement and the figure are not the same vintage.
